theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Why do many barbers use a straight razor with a changeable blade instead of a fixed-blade razor?
options: Changeable blades cut much faster, so each shave takes less time
Fixed blades are not allowed to be sharpened in a salon
A new blade can be used for each client, cutting infection risk
Changeable blades never cut the skin, however they are used

questions.stem: How many clients can one razor blade be used on?
options: One client only, then it goes in the sharps box
Two clients, as long as it is wiped clean with alcohol in between
As many as it stays sharp for
Up to a full day of clients

questions.stem: Why should the barber open the new blade's wrapper in front of the client?
options: So the client can check that the blade is sharp enough
Because blades must be opened near the client's face
So the barber can ask the client to load it
So the client can see that a fresh blade is being used

questions.stem: Where must a used razor blade be put?
options: In the general waste bin, wrapped in tissue
Straight into a sharps container
In a drawer, to dispose of at the end of the week
Back in its paper wrapper on the trolley

questions.stem: What is a sharps container?
options: A strong, puncture-proof, labelled box with a lid for used blades
A plastic bag that is tied shut when it is full
A cardboard shoe box kept under the shaving chair for used blades
A glass jar of disinfectant for soaking blades

questions.stem: When should a sharps container be closed and sent for disposal?
options: When it is full to the top and blades stick out
Only once a year, at the stock take
When it reaches the fill line marked on it
Whenever the barber has a spare moment

questions.stem: How should a full, closed sharps container be disposed of?
options: Put out with the salon's general rubbish for the weekly collection
Burned in the yard behind the salon
Emptied, and the blades used again for practice
Through an approved waste service, as local rules say

questions.stem: What is the safe way to take a used blade out of the razor?
options: Pull it out quickly with your bare fingertips and lay it down
Keep fingers clear of the edge and drop it into the sharps box
Bend it in half with your fingers so it cannot be used again
Hand it to the client to show him that it has been changed

questions.stem: What is the difference between cleaning and disinfecting a razor handle?
options: Cleaning removes dirt and hair; disinfecting kills most germs
Cleaning kills all germs; disinfecting only removes hair
There is no real difference, because the two words mean the same thing
Cleaning is done weekly; disinfecting is done once a year

questions.stem: What does sterilising do that disinfecting does not?
options: It removes hair and skin from the tool
It makes the blade sharper
It kills all germs, including spores
It stops the tool from rusting

questions.stem: What must be done to a razor handle before it is disinfected?
options: Dry it in the sun for an hour
Wrap it in a used towel
Nothing at all; it can go straight into the disinfectant as it is
Clean it with soap and water to remove hair and lather

questions.stem: How long must a tool stay in a disinfectant?
options: For the contact time given on the disinfectant label
For a quick dip of about one second, then dry it on a towel
Overnight, every night, whatever the label says
Until the disinfectant changes colour

questions.stem: Which items must be fresh for every face shave client?
options: The barber chair, the mirror and the floor mat
Towels, neck strip, gloves and razor blade
The sharps container and the steamer
The bottle of aftershave balm

questions.stem: How should shaving cream be taken from its tub or tube for each client?
options: By dipping the brush used on the last client into the tub
With bare fingers, straight into the tub, to save on spatulas
By sharing one bowl of lather among the day's clients
From a pump or with a clean spatula, never with a used brush

questions.stem: Why should the barber wear disposable gloves during a face shave?
options: To keep the barber's hands warm from the hot towels
So that the barber can grip the razor more loosely and safely
To protect both people if the skin is cut and bleeds
Because the lather would stain the barber's hands

questions.stem: Which of these is a contraindication, meaning the face shave must NOT go ahead?
options: A skin infection, such as impetigo, in the beard area
A thick, curly beard that has grown for a week or more
Skin that is a little dry on the cheeks
A client who has not been shaved by a barber before

questions.stem: A client has open sores on his chin. What should the barber do?
options: Shave over the sores lightly so they heal faster
Not shave, explain why tactfully, and suggest he sees a doctor
Cover the sores with extra lather and then shave the face as normal
Put aftershave on the sores and then shave the area

questions.stem: What is "barber's itch" (tinea barbae)?
options: A rash caused by using a blunt blade, which clears up within an hour
The normal itching felt after any close shave
An allergy to the barber's cologne
A fungal infection of the beard area that can spread to others

questions.stem: A client has a raised mole on his cheek. What should the barber do?
options: Shave over it firmly to make it flat
Remove it with the razor during the shave
Shave carefully around it and never cut over it
Put a strong chemical on it first so it shrinks before shaving

questions.stem: During the consultation, a client says he takes a medicine that thins his blood. Why does this matter?
options: Any small nick may bleed more and for longer
His beard will grow back much faster
The lather will not stick to his skin and will slide off quickly
His skin will become oily during the shave

questions.stem: What causes razor bumps (pseudofolliculitis barbae)?
options: Germs from the barber's chair and cape that get onto the skin
Curly hairs that curl back and grow into the skin
Using cold water instead of warm water on the beard
Shaving too slowly with a very sharp blade

questions.stem: A client often gets razor bumps. How should the barber change the shave?
options: Shave against the grain twice to get the closest possible shave
Press harder so every hair is cut below the skin
Use a blunt blade so the hairs are not cut short
Shave with the grain, not against it, and not too close

questions.stem: A client's razor bumps are red, swollen and have pus in them. What should the barber do?
options: Shave them off to remove the pus
Squeeze them before shaving
Not shave the area, and suggest he sees a doctor
Put on an extra hot towel, then shave the area as normal

questions.stem: Why is a consultation done before a face shave?
options: To learn his wishes and check the skin is safe to shave
To decide how much to charge for the hot towels
To find out where the client works and lives, for the records
To pass the time while the towel steamer heats up

questions.stem: Which question is useful in a face shave consultation?
options: How much do you earn each month?
Which other barber shop in town do you usually go to for a shave?
Do you want to buy a new razor today?
Have you had any skin problems or reactions after shaving before?

questions.stem: Before shaving, why does the barber look at and feel the direction the beard grows?
options: So he can count the number of hairs on each cheek
So he can shave with the grain on the first pass
So he can tell how old the client is
So he can choose the colour of the towel

questions.stem: How should the client be positioned in the chair for a face shave?
options: Sitting upright with his head bent forward and resting on his chest
Standing beside the basin so the lather can drip off
Gown and fresh towel on, chair reclined and head supported
Lying flat with no headrest so the neck is stretched

questions.stem: Why is a hot towel put on the beard before shaving?
options: To soften the hair and warm the skin, so the shave is easier
To kill all of the germs on the skin before the blade touches it
To dry the skin so that the blade grips
To make the hairs stand up stiff and hard

questions.stem: How should the barber check the heat of a hot towel before it touches the client?
options: Ask the client to touch it with his lips
Put it straight on the client's face and ask
Hold it up to the light to look at the steam
Test it on his own inner wrist

questions.stem: When placing a hot towel on the face, what must the barber make sure of?
options: The whole face, nose and mouth are covered tightly
The nose is left uncovered so the client can breathe
The towel is dripping wet so it stays hot longer
The towel stays on for at least an hour so the skin is very soft

questions.stem: Before using an electric hot towel steamer, what should the barber check?
options: The steamer is full of shaving cream
The cable runs across the walkway to the chair
The plug and cable are undamaged, and his hands are dry
The steamer is switched on with the door left open all day

questions.stem: A client has a long, full beard and wants a clean shave. What should the barber do first?
options: Trim it short with clippers before the hot towel
Shave it all off dry with long, firm strokes
Pull the long hairs out with tweezers first
Put on lots of extra lather and shave off the full length

questions.stem: The lather has dried on part of the face before that area is shaved. What should the barber do?
options: Shave the dry area anyway, as it saves a lot of time
Splash cold water on it and shave at once
Leave that part unshaved and tell no one
Apply fresh warm lather before shaving that area

questions.stem: When shaving, what is the purpose of the barber's free hand?
options: To hold the client's chin down hard so he cannot move
To stretch the skin gently so it is firm and smooth
To press the client's head firmly into the headrest
To hold the client's hand for comfort

questions.stem: At about what angle to the skin is the blade usually held?
options: Flat on the skin, at 0 degrees
Upright, at 90 degrees
A low angle, about 30 degrees
Steep, at about 75 degrees

questions.stem: In which direction is the first pass (first time over) of a face shave usually made?
options: With the grain, in the direction the hair grows
Against the grain, to get the closest shave first
In circles, to follow the shape of the face
Always downwards, whatever way the hair grows

questions.stem: Which strokes are best with a straight razor?
options: Long, heavy strokes pressed hard
Quick sawing strokes back and forth
Scraping strokes in many directions
Short, light, smooth strokes

questions.stem: "Freehand", "backhand" and "reverse freehand" are the names of what?
options: Types of shaving cream for different skin
Ways of holding the razor for different strokes
Kinds of towel used during each stage of a shave
Steps in cleaning the razor after use

questions.stem: Why should the barber ask the client not to talk or move while the razor is near his mouth?
options: Talking makes the lather go flat
The client might swallow the lather
A sudden movement could cause a cut
It is rude for a client to talk while the barber works

questions.stem: A client gets a small nick that bleeds. Wearing gloves, what should the barber do first?
options: Press a clean single-use cotton pad on it until it stops
Wipe it with the hot towel and carry on shaving
Rub the shared styptic pencil firmly over it
Blow on it to dry it, and ignore it until the shave is finished

questions.stem: After a client's cut has stopped bleeding, what should happen to the cotton and gloves used?
options: Left on the trolley until the end of the day
Rinsed under the tap and kept on the trolley for the next small cut
Dropped in the open bin by the front desk
Put in a sealed bag for clinical waste, as the Centre's rules say

questions.stem: Why must blood from a cut be handled with great care?
options: Blood stains the barber's uniform and cannot be washed out
Infections such as hepatitis B and HIV can spread through blood
Blood on the blade makes the razor go blunt very quickly indeed
The client may faint if he sees blood on the towel

questions.stem: After the shave, what is usually done to remove the last of the lather and soothe the skin?
options: Rub the face hard with a dry towel
Splash on a strong alcohol aftershave at once to sting the skin
Wipe with a warm damp towel, then apply a cool towel
Leave the lather on to dry by itself

questions.stem: Which aftershave product is best for a client with sensitive skin or small nicks?
options: A strong alcohol-based splash
A scented body spray
Neat surface disinfectant on a cloth
An alcohol-free, soothing balm

questions.stem: Which aftercare advice should a client be given after a face shave?
options: Scrub the face hard each night to stop bumps
Keep hands off, moisturise gently and protect from sun
Shave again at home the same evening for a closer finish
Put on strong perfume to close the pores

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What product, applied with single-use cotton, helps to stop the bleeding from a small razor nick?
What is the oil called that is put on the beard before the lather, to help the blade glide?
What is the brush called that is used to put lather on the beard?
Which type of disposable glove is widely used by barbers because it resists many chemicals and does not contain latex?
What is the paper or cotton strip put around the client's neck, under the gown, called?
Impetigo is a skin infection caused by which type of germ?
Cold sores on the lip are caused by which type of germ?
What is the sheet from the maker called that gives a disinfectant's hazards, first aid and safe storage?
What is the second pass of a shave called, made after the first pass to get a closer finish?
In which book or form should the barber write down any cut or injury that happens during a service?
What is the cover called that the client wears over his clothes during the shave?
What fresh item is put on the chair's headrest for each client?
What do the letters PPE stand for?
Which skin condition shows as red, dry, itchy patches and must not be shaved over when it is broken or weeping?
What do Jamaican barbers often call shaping the edge of the beard and hairline with the razor to give a clean, sharp line?

essays.stem: Explain the difference between cleaning, disinfecting and sterilising, and say how each is used for the tools and items in a face shave.
essays.modelAnswer: Cleaning means washing away dirt, hair, lather and grease with soap or detergent and water. It does not kill all germs, but it must always come first, because germs hide under dirt. Disinfecting means using an approved disinfectant, for the contact time on its label, to kill most germs on a cleaned surface or tool. Sterilising kills all germs, including spores, usually with special equipment such as an autoclave. In a face shave, the razor blade is single-use: it is never cleaned or reused, but goes straight into the sharps box. The razor handle, the bowl and the shaving brush are cleaned, then disinfected between clients, then dried and stored in a clean, covered place. The trolley, chair arms and headrest are cleaned and wiped with disinfectant. Towels are used once and washed hot before reuse, and the neck strip and gloves are thrown away.
markingPoints: Cleaning removes dirt and hair and must come first
Disinfecting kills most germs, using the label's contact time
Sterilising kills all germs, including spores
The blade is single-use and goes in the sharps box; handle, bowl and brush are cleaned then disinfected
Surfaces are disinfected; towels are used once and washed; neck strip and gloves are thrown away

essays.stem: Describe how a barber loads, uses and disposes of a single-use razor blade safely. Include the rules for the sharps container.
essays.modelAnswer: The barber washes his hands and puts on gloves. He checks that the razor handle has been cleaned and disinfected. In front of the client, he opens a new blade from its sealed wrapper, so the client can see it is fresh. He loads it into the handle as the maker's instructions say, holding it by the blunt parts and keeping his fingers away from the edge. During the shave, he keeps the razor closed when it is not in use and never puts it down open on the chair or the client. After the shave, he removes the blade carefully, without bending or snapping it with his fingers, and drops it straight into the sharps container. The sharps container is strong, puncture-proof, clearly labelled and kept close to the work area, out of reach of children. It is closed when it reaches the fill line and disposed of through an approved waste service.
markingPoints: Opens a new sealed blade in front of the client, for one client only
Loads it as the maker says, fingers away from the edge
Keeps the razor closed when not in use and never leaves it open
Removes the blade carefully and puts it straight into the sharps container
Sharps container: puncture-proof, labelled, closed at the fill line, disposed of by an approved service

essays.stem: Describe the consultation a barber carries out before a face shave. Name conditions that mean the shave must not go ahead, and conditions that mean it can go ahead with care.
essays.modelAnswer: The barber seats the client comfortably, checks his record, and asks what he wants: a full shave, a beard outline or a neck shave. He asks about allergies, sensitive skin, razor bumps, skin problems after past shaves, and any medicine or medical condition that matters, such as blood-thinning medicine. Then, with clean hands, he looks at and feels the skin and the direction of beard growth. The shave must not go ahead if there is a skin infection, such as impetigo, boils, infected razor bumps, barber's itch or cold sores, or open cuts, sores, a weeping rash or sunburn. The barber explains tactfully and suggests the client sees a doctor. The shave can go ahead with care where there are moles or skin tags, which are shaved around, old scars, mild razor bumps, or blood-thinning medicine, where any nick may bleed more. The barber notes the findings on the record.
markingPoints: Asks the client's wishes and checks the record
Asks about allergies, sensitive skin, razor bumps, medicine and medical conditions
Looks at and feels the skin and the direction of growth
Names conditions that stop the shave (infections, open cuts or sores, sunburn) and refers to a doctor
Names conditions that need care (moles, scars, mild bumps, blood thinners) and records the findings

essays.stem: Describe, step by step, how to prepare a client's skin and beard for a face shave.
essays.modelAnswer: First I gown the client, put on a fresh neck strip and towel, recline the chair and support his head on a fresh headrest cover. I wash my hands and put on gloves. If the beard is long, I trim it short with clean, disinfected clippers. I cleanse the skin gently to remove dirt and oil. Next I take a hot towel from the steamer, wring it out, and test its heat on my own inner wrist before it touches the client. I wrap it around the beard area, leaving the nose clear, and leave it for a short time to soften the hair and warm the skin. I remove the towel and apply a little pre-shave oil, if the client has no allergy to it. Then I apply warm lather from a pump or clean spatula, using a clean brush or gloved hands with circular movements to lift the hairs. I keep the lather moist and relather any area that dries.
markingPoints: Prepares the client: gown, neck strip, towel, reclined chair, fresh headrest cover
Trims a long beard first and cleanses the skin
Tests the hot towel on own inner wrist and leaves the nose clear
Applies pre-shave oil if suitable
Applies lather hygienically with circular movements and relathers if it dries

essays.stem: Describe how a barber carries out the shave itself, from the first stroke to the second time over, keeping the client safe.
essays.modelAnswer: Before starting, I check the direction of growth in each area, because it can change on the neck and under the jaw. I tell the client I am starting and ask him to keep still and not talk while the razor is near his mouth. I use the right hold for each stroke, such as freehand or backhand. With my free hand, using dry fingertips, I stretch the skin gently so it is firm. I hold the blade at a low angle, about 30 degrees, and use short, light, smooth strokes, never sawing or pressing hard. The first time over is with the grain, in the direction the hair grows. I work in a set order around the face and neck, wiping the lather off the blade onto a clean tissue. I take extra care around the nostrils, lips, jawline and Adam's apple. If the skin is calm, I relather and do a second time over across the grain, but not against the grain on sensitive or bump-prone skin.
markingPoints: Checks growth direction in each area and asks the client to keep still
Uses correct razor holds and stretches the skin with the free hand
Low blade angle with short, light strokes
First time over with the grain, in a set order, wiping the blade on a clean tissue
Extra care at nose, lips and neck; second time over across the grain only if the skin allows

essays.stem: Many clients with tightly curled beard hair get razor bumps (pseudofolliculitis barbae). Explain what causes them, how a barber adapts the shave, and what advice to give.
essays.modelAnswer: Razor bumps happen when a curly hair is cut very short and then curls back into the skin, or grows sideways under it. The skin reacts as if the hair were a splinter, making red, itchy, sometimes painful bumps. They are common in men with tightly curled beards. If the bumps are infected, swollen or full of pus, the barber must not shave the area and should advise the client to see a doctor. If they are mild, the barber can adapt the shave. He softens the beard well with a hot towel and lather, shaves only with the grain, does not stretch the skin too tightly, and avoids going against the grain or shaving too close. Sometimes it is better to leave a short stubble with a trimmer. He should advise the client to exfoliate gently, use a soothing, alcohol-free product, not pick or squeeze bumps, and see a doctor if they get worse.
markingPoints: Cause: short, curly hairs curl back or grow into the skin
Infected or pus-filled bumps: no shave, refer to a doctor
Adapted shave: well softened, with the grain, skin not over-stretched, not too close
May leave short stubble with a trimmer
Advice: gentle exfoliation, soothing product, no picking, see a doctor if worse

essays.stem: During a face shave, the client is nicked and the cut bleeds. Describe exactly what the barber should do.
essays.modelAnswer: The barber stops shaving at once, stays calm and tells the client what has happened. He makes sure his gloves are on and are not torn. He presses a clean, single-use cotton pad or tissue on the cut until the bleeding stops. Then he applies a styptic powder or liquid with a fresh piece of cotton, never with a shared styptic pencil. He does not put alcohol-based products on the cut. If the bleeding will not stop, or the cut is deep, he gets first-aid help and medical advice. All the cotton, tissues and gloves with blood on them go into a sealed bag and are disposed of as clinical waste, as the Centre's rules say. The blade goes in the sharps box. He cleans and disinfects any surface with blood on it, washes his hands, and puts on fresh gloves before carrying on. He writes the injury in the accident book and tells the supervisor.
markingPoints: Stops, stays calm, checks his gloves are intact
Presses a clean single-use pad on the cut until bleeding stops
Applies styptic with fresh cotton, never a shared pencil, and gets help if bleeding continues
Bags blood-stained items as clinical waste and disinfects surfaces
Washes hands, changes gloves and records the injury

essays.stem: Describe how a barber finishes a face shave, and the aftercare advice he gives the client.
essays.modelAnswer: When the shave is complete, the barber wipes away the last of the lather with a warm, damp towel. He checks the face and neck by sight and touch for any missed hairs or nicks, and deals with any nick hygienically. He then places a cool towel on the face to soothe and refresh the skin. He applies an aftershave balm or toner that suits the skin: an alcohol-free, soothing product for sensitive skin or any small nicks. He removes the neck strip and towel, brushes away loose hairs, raises the chair and shows the client the result in a mirror. For aftercare, he advises the client not to touch or scratch the shaved area, to use a gentle moisturiser, to protect the skin from strong sun, and to avoid strongly scented products for the rest of the day. If the client gets razor bumps, he advises gentle exfoliation in the following days and a doctor if any spot becomes infected.
markingPoints: Removes lather with a warm damp towel and checks for missed hairs or nicks
Uses a cool towel to soothe the skin
Applies a suitable aftershave, alcohol-free for sensitive skin
Removes the neck strip and towel and shows the result
Gives aftercare: no touching, moisturise, sun protection, avoid strong scents, see a doctor if infected

essays.stem: Describe how a barber cleans up the shaving area after a client, ready for the next one.
essays.modelAnswer: With gloves still on, the barber removes the used blade carefully and drops it straight into the sharps container. He puts used towels and the gown in the laundry bin, to be washed hot. The neck strip, headrest cover, cotton and tissues go in the bin, and anything with blood on it goes in a sealed clinical waste bag. He washes the razor handle, bowl and shaving brush with soap and water to remove hair and lather, then disinfects them for the contact time on the disinfectant's label, rinses them if the label says so, dries them and stores them covered. He wipes the chair, headrest, arm rests and trolley with disinfectant, and sweeps up any hair. He takes off his gloves, puts them in the bin and washes his hands. Finally he checks that the sharps container is below its fill line, refills supplies, and lays out fresh towels and a new blade, still sealed, for the next client.
markingPoints: Puts the used blade straight into the sharps container
Sends towels and gown to the laundry and bins single-use items, with blood-stained items as clinical waste
Cleans, then disinfects, the handle, bowl and brush for the label's contact time, and stores them covered
Disinfects the chair, headrest and trolley and sweeps up hair
Removes gloves, washes hands, checks the sharps box and resets the station

essays.stem: Explain how a barber keeps safe when using disinfectants and other chemicals, and the electrical equipment, in the shaving area.
essays.modelAnswer: For chemicals, the barber reads the label and the safety data sheet before using a disinfectant or cleaner, and follows the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules. He mixes it only to the strength on the label, with water, and never mixes two chemicals together. He wears gloves, and eye protection if there is a risk of splashes, and uses it in a well-ventilated area. Chemicals are kept in their labelled containers, with lids closed, in a cool place away from heat, food and clients. If a chemical splashes in the eyes, he rinses them with plenty of clean running water and gets medical help. For electrical equipment, such as the towel steamer and clippers, he checks the plug and cable for damage before use, keeps water away from them, uses them only with dry hands, and keeps cables out of walkways. Faulty equipment is unplugged, labelled and reported, not used.
markingPoints: Reads the label and SDS and follows the maker's instructions
Correct dilution and never mixes chemicals
Wears gloves (and eye protection), uses good ventilation and stores chemicals safely
First aid: rinses eyes with running water and gets medical help
Electrical: checks plug and cable, dry hands, cables tidy, faulty items labelled and reported

practical1.title: Set up a hygienic shaving station, handle blades safely, check for contraindications and practise razor strokes on a balloon
practical1.brief: As a group, set up one shaving station in the Centre's barbering area and practise the safe, hygienic steps of a face shave, without shaving a person. First, together, clean and disinfect the chair, headrest and trolley, and lay out the tools and fresh items for one client, with a sharps container within reach. Then every member takes a turn at each task while the assessor watches: (1) a consultation with a partner, using a contraindication card from the assessor (for example impetigo, infected razor bumps, a raised mole, a client on blood-thinning medicine, healthy skin), filling in a consultation form and deciding whether the shave can go ahead, go ahead with care, or must not go ahead and the client be referred to a doctor; (2) preparing a hot towel from the steamer and testing its heat on their own inner wrist; (3) opening a new blade in front of the "client", loading it into the razor as the maker says, and then removing it and putting it straight into the sharps container; (4) lathering a blown-up balloon with a pump or spatula and shaving it clean, using freehand and backhand strokes and a gently stretched surface, without bursting it; (5) cleaning and disinfecting the razor handle, bowl and brush for the label's contact time. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: A barber chair with headrest, a trolley and a hot towel steamer
A changeable-blade straight razor handle and sealed single-use blades
Shaving cream in a pump or tub, single-use spatulas, a shaving brush and bowl
Towels, neck strips, headrest covers, nitrile gloves and tissues
An approved disinfectant with its safety data sheet, and cleaning brushes
Contraindication cards and consultation forms from the assessor
photos: The cleaned shaving station with tools, fresh items and the sharps container laid out
Each member's completed consultation form with their decision
A member testing a hot towel on their inner wrist
A new blade being opened from its sealed wrapper and loaded
A used blade going into the sharps container
Each member's lathered balloon before shaving
Each member's balloon shaved clean and unburst
The razor handle, bowl and brush in disinfectant, and then stored clean and dry
checklist: Washed hands and wore gloves, and set up a clean station with fresh items
Asked suitable consultation questions and recorded the findings
Made the right decision for the contraindication card, and referred to a doctor where needed
Tested the hot towel heat on their own inner wrist
Opened a new blade in front of the client and loaded it safely, fingers clear of the edge
Put the used blade straight into the sharps container
Lathered hygienically and shaved the balloon with correct holds, light strokes and a low angle
Cleaned and then disinfected the tools for the label's contact time
safety: Handle blades by the blunt parts only; never pass an open razor to another person
Put every used blade straight into the sharps container; if anyone is cut, stop, apply first aid and report it
Test every hot towel on your inner wrist; keep the steamer's cable tidy and use it with dry hands
Use the disinfectant as the label and safety data sheet say, with gloves and good ventilation, and never mix chemicals
Follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules for every tool

practical2.title: Perform a full face shave on a model
practical2.brief: As a group, carry out full face shaves on adult models in the Centre's barbering area, under the assessor's close supervision. Each model must agree in writing and have a few days' beard growth, and the assessor checks each model's skin before any work starts. Every member performs one complete face shave while the other members help: one prepares the hot towels, one records the consultation and the times, and one takes the photos. Each member: carries out the consultation and checks for contraindications; prepares the client with a gown, neck strip, fresh towel and headrest cover; trims the beard first if it is long; prepares the skin with a hot towel tested on their inner wrist, pre-shave oil if suitable, and lather; opens a new blade in front of the model; shaves the face and neck with the grain, using correct holds, a stretched skin and light strokes, and does a second time over only if the skin allows; finishes with a warm then cool towel and a suitable aftershave; gives aftercare advice; and then puts the blade in the sharps container and cleans and disinfects the station for the next member. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Photos show only the work area (the jaw, cheek or neck), never the eyes or the whole face, unless the model agrees and the Centre allows it. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: A barber chair with headrest, a trolley, a hot towel steamer and clippers or a trimmer
A changeable-blade straight razor handle and a sealed single-use blade for each model
A sharps container and clinical waste bags
Cleanser, pre-shave oil, shaving cream in a pump or tub with spatulas, a shaving brush and bowl
Fresh towels, gowns, neck strips, headrest covers, nitrile gloves, tissues and cotton pads
Styptic powder or liquid, an alcohol-free aftershave balm and an approved disinfectant
Consultation forms, model consent forms and aftercare leaflets
A first-aid kit and the accident book
photos: The prepared station before each shave, with a sealed blade and the sharps container
Each member's completed consultation form and the model's signed consent
The hot towel on the beard area, nose left clear (work area only)
The beard area lathered (jaw, cheek or neck only)
The shave in progress, showing the skin being stretched (work area only)
The finished shave of the cheek and neck (work area only)
The used blade going into the sharps container
The station cleaned and disinfected after each shave
checklist: Carried out a full consultation and checked the skin for contraindications
Prepared the client and the station hygienically, with fresh items and gloves
Tested the hot towel on their own inner wrist and left the nose clear
Lathered hygienically and kept the lather moist
Opened a new blade in front of the model and handled the razor safely throughout
Shaved with the grain using correct holds, a stretched skin, a low angle and light strokes
Did a second time over only where the skin allowed, and dealt correctly with any nick
Finished with warm and cool towels and a suitable aftershave, and gave aftercare advice
Put the blade in the sharps container and cleaned and disinfected the station
safety: Stop and do not shave if any contraindication is found; refer the model to a doctor
Wear gloves throughout; treat any nick with a clean single-use pad and styptic, bag blood-stained items as clinical waste and record it
Open a new blade for each model and put it straight into the sharps container after use
Test every hot towel on your inner wrist and keep the nose clear
Never leave an open razor on the chair, trolley or model; keep the steamer cable tidy and use it with dry hands
Follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules, and work only while the assessor is watching
